initiative.title: Cloud sessions
initiative.summary: Push locally recorded sessions to an owner-only Cloudflare-hosted store so they can be reviewed in a browser and processed by agents from any machine.
initiative.next_action: Review shape open choices, then start M1 (cloud copy on disk).

sources.anchor: Session output; Edited sessions; Drawing on the video
du per part: mp4 26-41MB, pages 0-12MB, audio.wav 3-7MB, jsonl <200KB
workers-oauth-provider; Access as IdP; createMcpHandler stateless; remote-mcp-cf-access template

claims.statement: Record on one computer, then view and have an agent process the session from a different computer or the cloud.
One owner signs in. The owner can also hand out private per-session share links to people without accounts.
claims.notes: Whether anyone besides the owner ever views is unasked.

claims.statement: Sessions are local by default and pushed to the cloud explicitly.
The cloud viewer has review parity with the native viewer.
claims.notes: Scoped in round 2: cuts, drawings, joins; canvas later.

claims.statement: Advanced features (joining, cutting, canvas building) may be limited in the cloud. Keeping annotation would be nice.
claims.notes: Annotating in the cloud is out for the first release because the cloud is read-only (round 1). Drawings made on the Mac are still shown.

claims.statement: Agents read sessions from two places: Claude Code on another Mac and cloud agents. Both need access without the recording Mac.
claims.notes: Durable intent: an agent elsewhere can read a session. The mechanism is undecided.

claims.statement: Target Cloudflare and use its native services. Coolify with Docker Compose and a volume is the known fallback.
claims.notes: The user has no Cloudflare account yet.

claims.statement: Sessions are 40-50 MB, dominated by recording.mp4. session.json bundles the viewer data. viewer.html does not render edits, annotations or the canvas.
Saved pages and narration may hold sensitive content, so what gets uploaded is a policy choice.
The cloud is a read-only mirror of what the Mac pushed. Changes happen on the Mac, and you push again.
A second Mac pulling cloud sessions into its native library comes later.
Push is a per-session button. Later edits on the Mac mark the cloud copy stale until you push again.
Upload video, narration, logs and saved pages, with a size cap on saved pages so they never dwarf the video.
claims.notes: The cap value is a provisional default. audio.wav is redundant with the mp4 audio track.

claims.statement: Share links are view-only, unguessable, per session, with no expiry by default, and revocable.
The cloud viewer must play edited sessions with cuts applied, show drawings on the video, and play joined sessions. The canvas view can wait.
Agents use sessions to turn marks into fixes or tickets, and need to see the video at moments that may have no mark.
Budget is up to about $5/month. The site runs on a domain the user owns, moved to Cloudflare DNS.
Trashing a pushed session on the Mac asks whether to delete the cloud copy as well.
Cross-session search and questions like "what happened" are not first-release agent jobs.

shape.appetite: One Worker, one R2 bucket, D1, KV, and a push command in the app. No cloud-side processing except frame extraction.
shape.problem: Sessions are reachable only on the recording Mac. Viewing elsewhere and agent processing need a private, owned cloud copy.
shape.recommended_shape: Flatten on the Mac (EditMap composition export, rendered drawing PNGs, edited-time session.json, thumbs) into a self-contained cloud copy. One Cloudflare Worker serves the library, viewer, share pages and a remote MCP from R2 and D1, behind Access.
success_moves: Flatten cuts and joins at push using EditMap.composition, so no cloud code knows about edits
Render drawings with Annotation.Renderer to PNG overlays, avoiding a second JS renderer
One viewer template for local viewer.html and the cloud
Thumbs every 2 s serve viewer hover and act as the local fake for get_frame
Content-hashed manifest makes re-push incremental and drives the out-of-date badge
Identity, Store and Frames seams let the Worker run fully on wrangler dev

first_proof.question: Does a flattened cloud copy keep cuts, joins, drawings and mark times faithful to the app?
first_proof.artifact: --cloud-bundle output for a real edited and annotated session, played by the shared viewer from disk and then from wrangler dev
first_proof.decision_rule: If cut points, mark times and drawing windows match the app within one frame, keep flatten-on-push. If not, switch to client-side segment stepping before building further.

rabbit_holes: Rendering edits or joins in the browser
open_decisions: Agents and shares never see cut footage (treated as intended)
Saved-page budget default: max(10 MB, half the video)

deployment_surfaces: Cloudflare Workers + R2 + D1 + KV on user domain, behind Access (new)

milestones.title: The cloud copy plays from disk
milestones.outcome: --cloud-bundle writes a self-contained folder that the shared viewer plays with cuts, joins and drawings matching the app.
milestones.proof: --self-test cloud-bundle; one real edited, annotated session compared against the app within one frame
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: A local export command exists; nothing uploads; viewer.html still works embedded.
milestones.rollback: Remove the command; session folders are untouched (output goes to a chosen folder).

milestones.title: Push to a local cloud and browse it
milestones.outcome: The app pushes a session to the Worker on wrangler dev, and it plays in the browser with seeking; re-push sends only changed files.
milestones.proof: vitest push/commit/Range/delete; app push to localhost viewed in the browser pane
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Cloud usable locally; push hidden unless a cloud URL is configured.
milestones.rollback: Unset the cloud URL; delete exports/cloud.json.

milestones.title: Agents read sessions locally over MCP
milestones.outcome: Claude Code connected to the local Worker reads marks and fetches a frame at any time.
milestones.proof: MCP contract tests on seeded Miniflare; Inspector and claude mcp add run
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: MCP served locally with the thumbs frames adapter.

milestones.title: Live on your domain
milestones.outcome: Sessions play at sessions.<domain> behind Access, pushed from the app with a service token.
milestones.proof: Signed-out request blocked; phone viewing after sign-in; Media Transformations spike result recorded
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Live cloud for the owner; MCP live but unauthenticated route disabled until m5.
milestones.rollback: Disable the Worker route or Access app; Mac copies are untouched.

milestones.title: Agents from anywhere
milestones.outcome: Claude Code on another machine and a cloud agent sign in and use the MCP while the recording Mac sleeps.
milestones.proof: Both clients fetch get_frame for the same moment
milestones.rollback: Disable /mcp; viewer and push keep working.

milestones.title: Sharing and lifecycle
milestones.outcome: Revocable view-only share links; trashing a pushed session asks about the cloud copy.
milestones.proof: vitest share/revoke; signed-out browser check; trash prompt in the app
milestones.rollback: Revoke all shares; remove the Bypass policy.

questions.question: Who besides you ever looks at a cloud session?
questions.effect: Owner-only login plus per-session private share links for people without accounts.

questions.question: Where does the processing agent run?
questions.answer: Claude Code on another Mac, and cloud agents
questions.effect: Needs both a local-friendly route and a remote route (remote MCP or HTTP API).

questions.question: Can you change a session from the cloud?
questions.effect: Cloud mirrors pushes; no sync-back. Cloud annotation drops out of first release.

questions.question: Should a second Mac pull cloud sessions into its library?
questions.effect: Below the cut line; keep the stored format download-friendly.

questions.question: How does a session get to the cloud and stay current?
questions.effect: Explicit push; app flags stale cloud copy; re-push replaces.

questions.question: Which parts go up?
questions.answer: Video, narration audio; saved pages and raw logs OK up to some size limit — no feel for the limit
questions.effect: Provisional default: upload all but audio.wav (redundant with mp4); logs always; saved pages under a per-session cap, largest dropped first, skipped ones listed.

questions.question: What should a share link do?
questions.effect: Unguessable per-session link, no default expiry, owner can revoke. Not an agent credential.

questions.question: Parity bar for first release?
questions.answer: Cuts applied, drawings on video, joined sessions
questions.effect: Canvas view is below the cut line. Joined sessions need their sources uploaded or resolved at push.

questions.question: What will agents mostly do with a session?
questions.answer: Marks to fixes/tickets; look at the video
questions.effect: Agent route serves mark Markdown, images, page context, and frames at arbitrary times. Cross-session search and Q&A are below the line.

questions.question: Monthly bill?
questions.effect: Workers Paid allowed; Stream-class spend not assumed.

questions.question: Address?
questions.effect: Zone moves to Cloudflare DNS; custom hostname enables Access and Media Transformations.

questions.question: Lifecycle check
questions.effect: Trashing a pushed session prompts to delete the cloud copy too; otherwise lifecycles are independent.
